limitations_and_boundaries: The Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test is underpowered due to small sample size (6 experimental settings).
GraphSAGE focuses on feature-rich graphs but can use structural features; performance on graphs without any features is not explicitly evaluated.
The pooling aggregator uses a simple single-layer MLP before max-pooling; deeper architectures are not explored.
The LSTM aggregator is applied to unordered neighbor sets, which may not be optimal.
Hyperparameter tuning was performed on subsets of citation and Reddit data, which may not generalize to other domains.
The PPI dataset results may be further improved with task-specific hyperparameter optimization and new training techniques (as noted in follow-up work).

research_questions.statement: Can we design an inductive framework that leverages node features to efficiently generate embeddings for previously unseen nodes?

provenance.text_excerpt: Here we present GraphSAGE, a general inductive framework that leverages node feature information (e.g., text attributes) to efﬁciently generate node embeddings for previously unseen data.

claims.statement: GraphSAGE is a general inductive framework that leverages node feature information to efficiently generate node embeddings for previously unseen data.

experiments_or_tasks: Propose GraphSAGE, a general inductive framework that learns a function to generate node embeddings by sampling and aggregating features from a node's local neighborhood.

methods.name: GraphSAGE
methods.protocol_description: GraphSAGE trains a set of aggregator functions that aggregate feature information from a node's local neighborhood at different search depths. At inference, embeddings for unseen nodes are generated by applying the learned aggregation functions. The framework can be trained with an unsupervised loss or a supervised cross-entropy loss.

study_units.name: GraphSAGE framework proposal

claims.statement: GraphSAGE significantly outperforms baseline approaches on inductive node classification benchmarks.

claims.statement: Using K=2 provides a good trade-off between accuracy and runtime.

provenance.text_excerpt: the new aggregator architectures we propose provide significant gains (7.4% on average) compared to an aggregator inspired by graph convolutional networks

methods.name: GraphSAGE variants
methods.protocol_description: GraphSAGE with different aggregator functions: GraphSAGE-GCN (convolutional), GraphSAGE-mean, GraphSAGE-LSTM, GraphSAGE-pool. Unsupervised variants trained with loss in Equation (1); supervised variants trained on classification cross-entropy loss. All use ReLU non-linearity, K=2, neighborhood sample sizes S1=25 and S2=10. Hyperparameters swept over same set for all variants, chosen by validation performance.

methods.name: Baselines
methods.protocol_description: Random classifier, logistic regression feature-based classifier (ignores graph structure), DeepWalk algorithm (online training for new test nodes), concatenation of raw features and DeepWalk embeddings. DeepWalk uses vanilla gradient descent optimizer; other models use Adam optimizer.
